source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's NVA8 campus in Sterling, Virginia publishes 24 MW of IT capacity and 154,230 square feet of technical space, and that is the whole of its public record.

The two numbers are a nameplate power figure and a floor area, not a machine count. At 40 kW per rack, 24 MW of IT load implies roughly 600 racks, and at 100 kW per rack it implies roughly 240, but CyrusOne publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant list, so any rack figure is an outside assumption. The square footage works out to about 156 watts per square foot across the technical space, a density consistent with a high-density hall without proving one.

Within Virginia the campus ranks 21st of the 29 facilities that publish a megawatt figure, and those 29 total 2,563.4 MW, making NVA8 about 0.9 percent of the published state capacity. Virginia has 376 mapped facilities, most publishing nothing, so the real state total is larger and this rank sits inside a partial list. The operator also publishes no certifications, no address, and no postal code, so nothing here establishes what standards the facility meets or what workloads it can host.

For AI specifically, the useful reading is that this is a mid-sized published load in the country's largest concentrated data center market, and its weight depends on capacity and tenant facts the operator has not disclosed.
